newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYOIL ENDS DOWN, MEAL UP WITH SOYBEANS.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYOIL ENDS DOWN, MEAL UP WITH SOYBEANS.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended lower Wednesday on commercial selling, while soymeal futures borrowed strength from soybeans to end higher, traders said.
Nearby soymeal contracts rallied sharply into the close in line with the gains in August soybeans. August ended up 35-1/4 cents per bushel on tight near-term supplies of soybeans, traders said.
Some of the weakness in soyoil was also linked to ideas the market was overbought following sharp gains on Wednesday.
Talk of Chinese interest in U.S. soyoil lingered in the market, but cash and export sources couldn't confirm sales.
Traders in Argentina said interest in soyoil was shifting to the U.S. Gulf as U.S. prices become more competitive with those in South America.
On Wednesday, the Commodity Credit Corporation said it will tender on August 18 for 3,945 tonnes of sunoil for shipment to Bosnia and Georgia for October/November shipment.
December soyoil ended down 0.12 cent per lb at 22.50, and other months were down 0.09 to 0.17. December soymeal ended up $1.80 at $201.10 per ton, with other contracts up $5.10 to off $1.50.
Traders expect light weekly soyoil sales and heavy new crop soymeal sales when USDA releases export sales data on Thursday at 0730 CDT.
Estimates for soyoil were 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes, and estimates for new crop soymeal were for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes. Traders estimated old crop soymeal sales at 30,000 to 50,000 tonnes.
On the day in soyoil trade, ADM sold 100 lots of October and 200 lots of December and Cargill sold 300 lots of December. Term Commodities bought 200 lots September, pit sources said.
In soymeal trade, Refco bought 800 lots December and 100 lots of September and Continental Grain bought 300 lots December and 100 lots September.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 23,000 lots, against Tuesday's 26,358. Soyoil volume was pegged at 10,000 lots against Tuesday's 15,643.
